previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and a history of gastrointestinal bleeding presented with generalized weakness and chest pain after missing dialysis and experiencing severe diarrhea. He was found to have life-threatening hyperkalemia, which was treated with emergency dialysis. The chest pain was determined to be non-cardiac, likely musculoskeletal, with imaging showing a possible fracture of the left eighth rib. An inpatient capsule endoscopy was performed due to prior failed outpatient attempts, with results pending at discharge. His hand pain, following a fall, was attributed to soft tissue injury or gout flare. He remained stable throughout the admission, with improvement in electrolytes and symptoms, and was discharged home with follow-up plans for GI evaluation, blood sugar monitoring, and medication management.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Altered mental status, history of fall and head strike.  Question
intracranial hemorrhage, pneumonia, cervical spine injury.

COMPARISONS:  CT head from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial imaging was obtained through the brain without the
administration of intravenous contrast material.  Coronal and sagittal
reformats were completed.

FINDINGS:  There is no acute intracranial hemorrhage, edema, mass effect or
large territorial infarction.  The ventricles and sulci are prominent
consistent with atrophy.  There is a small mucus retention cyst within the
right maxillary sinus.  A prior left inferior orbital wall fracture with
herniation of fat and tenting of the inferior rectus muscle into the left
maxillary sinus is stable.  A hyperdense right occipital soft tissue lesion
measuring 3.4 x 1.0 cm is unchanged since the previous exam.  A left occipital
scalp lipoma is noted.  There are no acute fractures.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial process.

INDICATION:  History of fall and head strike with altered mental status. 
Evaluate for cervical spine injury.

COMPARISONS:  CT cervical spine from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial imaging was obtained through the cervical spine
without the administration of intravenous contrast material.  Coronal and
sagittal reformats were completed.

FINDINGS:  There is no acute fracture, traumatic malalignment or prevertebral
soft tissue swelling.  The vertebral body heights are maintained.  There are
mild multilevel degenerative changes with progression of endplate sclerosis at
the C3 compared to the prior exam.  A right paracentral disc bulge at C3-C4
causes mild central canal and right neural foraminal narrowing, likely similar
to the prior exam.  A disc bulge at C5-C6 also indents the ventral thecal sac.
There is no significant canal stenosis at this level.  There are degenerative
changes and fusion of the left facets at C2 and C3.

The visualized soft tissues, including the thyroid gland are unremarkable. 
The lung apices demonstrate mild centrilobular emphysema.  Again seen is a
hyperdense scalp lesion within the right occipital area and a left occipital
scalp lipoma.

IMPRESSION:  No acute fracture or traumatic malalignment.  Mild multilevel
degenerative changes with canal narrowing at C3 and C4 as seen previously.

HISTORY:  Fall with left arm and leg pain.

TECHNIQUE:  AP view of the pelvis, 2 views of the left hip, and 2 views of the
left knee.

COMPARISON:  Report from the left hip radiograph ___.  Images are not
available for direct comparison.

FINDINGS:

There is no acute fracture or dislocation within the pelvis or left hip.  Mild
degenerative changes are present at both hips joints.  Penile prosthesis is
noted.  There are diffuse vascular calcifications.  No diastasis of the pubic
symphysis or sacroiliac joints is present.

Within the knee, there are mild degenerative changes in all 3 compartments of
the knee with osteophytic spurring.  No joint effusion is present.  There is a
small superior patellar enthesophyte.  Vascular calcifications are present.

IMPRESSION:

No acute fracture or dislocation within the left hip or knee.

HISTORY:  Altered mental status, fall, head strike.

TECHNIQUE:  Supine AP view of the chest.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:

Heart size is moderate to severely enlarged but unchanged.  The mediastinal
contours are stable.  There is mild pulmonary edema, not substantially changed
from the prior exam.  A small right pleural effusion persists.  No
pneumothorax is identified, and there is no left-sided pleural effusion.  No
new displaced rib fracture is clearly visualized.  Multilevel degenerative
changes are noted in the thoracic spine.

IMPRESSION:

Mild pulmonary edema and small right pleural effusion, not substantially
changed from the prior exam.

HISTORY:  Fall with left arm and leg pain.

TECHNIQUE:  3 views of the left elbow and 3 views of the left wrist.

COMPARISON:  Left wrist radiographs ___.

FINDINGS:

There is no acute fracture or dislocation.  A joint effusion is not seen
within the left elbow.  No suspicious lytic or sclerotic osseous abnormalities
seen.  Diffuse vascular calcifications are noted.  Minimal osteoarthritis is
again noted within the ___ CMC and triscaphe joints.

IMPRESSION:

No acute fracture or dislocation within the left elbow or wrist.

HISTORY:  ___ man with end-stage renal disease on dialysis.  Left
lower extremity swelling.  Question DVT.  

COMPARISON:  None 

FINDINGS: Gray scale and color Doppler ultrasound was performed of the left
common femoral, superficial femoral, popliteal, posterior tibial and peroneal
veins.  There is normal flow, augmentation and compressibility.  

IMPRESSION: No evidence of DVT in the left lower extremity.
